Today, they sell commercialized sets with step-by-step instructions on how to simply replicate things from Hollywood movies; no imagination, just follow directions.

You know, I've played with Lego for over 40 years. I play with my kid now - and I still buy sets now and then for myself.

Lego has always had the step by step instructions - its supposed to be an age-grade easy toy for kids. And while it seems like all Lego sells anymore are the commercialized sets for building specific things, Lego still does sell plenty of 'creative' sets with no specific set-goals.

The ideas behind the 'commercialized' sets is: yes, first you build the set according to the instructions. But then most kids, after a time, will modify, or tear down the sets to make new things.

Lego is still very much about imagination. But it's also about teaching kids process and reward for effort.
